title: Tenant KV eviction prober with SLO-sensing soft-quota for continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In multi-tenant continuous batching the KV cache can be dominated by a few noisy tenants which drives GPU memory pressure, preemptions, and SLO violations for latency-sensitive tenants. Existing approaches either hard-evict aggressively (causes quality regressions and repeated cold-start KV misses) or favor long residency (causes OOM/preemption cascades). We need a middle ground: a low-latency-aware, soft-quota eviction controller that probes eviction impact and adapts preemption budgets per tenant while preserving fairness across SLO tiers.

Scope: implement a tenant-level KV eviction prober that: (1) assigns a soft-resident quota per tenant derived from recent sequence-length and cache hit-rate signals, (2) runs controlled eviction probes that evict a small delta and measure short-term latency/regressions, (3) computes per-tenant soft-preemption quotas and interrupt quanta to use in the preemptor, and (4) exposes metrics and a rollout plan. This targets continuous-batching runtime only (no control-plane changes).

Design summary:
- Soft quota calculation: sliding-window estimate of working-set bytes = recent top-K attention-key footprint + prefix reuse rate. Soft quota is a percentile (e.g., 75th) scaled by tenant SLO weight.
- Probe mechanism: periodically evict 2-5% of a tenant's least-recently-used KV pages and trace downstream token latency and model-output token error (via existing quality checks). If degradation > threshold, mark probe as harmful and increase grace retention. If safe, reduce quota and release memory to other tenants.
- Integration with preemptor: preemption scheduler will consult soft-preemption budget per tenant. Budgets are tokenized into interrupt quanta (ms or token-budget) allowing short interrupts that respect latency SLOs.
- Fairness policy: tie tenant budgets to SLO tier and recent SLA compliance; use exponential backoff on repeated harmful probes to avoid oscillation.

Trade-offs considered: aggressive eviction improves throughput and reduces OOM risk but increases cold-start KV misses and increases downstream compute; probe approach adds complexity and temporary measurement noise; conservative quotas preserve QoE but increase preemptions and resource contention. Chosen approach biases slightly conservative for P0/P1 customers and more aggressive reclamation for best-effort tenants.

Monitoring and metrics: per-tenant KV-residency, probe-success-rate, probe-latency-delta, preemption-frequency, SLO-latency-p50/p95/p99, GPU memory headroom. Add dashboard in Console under runtime-scheduling-v2.

Rollout plan: feature-flag gated. Start with internal canary pool (dev/dedicated infra) for 2 weeks, then 5% production with P0 tenants excluded, observe metrics for 7 days, iterate on thresholds, then 25% and full rollout.

Docs & artifacts (drafts): Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/RTS-eviction-prober, design diagram: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/RTS-evict-prober, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2871, load tests: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/runtime-scheduling/eviction-prober-experiments
acceptance_criteria: Soft-quota calculator returns per-tenant quota and is traceable via metrics
Probe mechanism can evict a configurable delta and emit probe-success/fail events
Preemptor consults soft-preemption budget and respects interrupt quanta in continuous batching path
End-to-end integration tests that simulate 3 tenants (P0, P2, best-effort) show no >5% p95 latency regression for P0 under typical load
Dashboard panels created and show probe and quota metrics
Feature flag and rollout steps documented and tested in canary
